title: Concrete eight-GPU H3 planning estimate from existing stage evidence

answer.central: Plan around145 videos/hour:8.1x the current200.346-second cold result. Use about115/hour for a downside capacity budget and175/hour as an optimistic engineering target. These are planning scenarios, not measured results or a statistical confidence interval.
answer.matched_warm: Central gain is7.05x versus an estimated174.7-second warm workstation, or7.42x versus an estimated183.9-second warm single target-SKU GPU. Greater than8x matched-warm scaling is not the central expectation.
answer.architecture: Five dedicated transformer GPUs and three GPUs sharing preparation/VAE work; persistent stage models, independent chunk queues and asynchronous CPU encoding/validation.
answer.purchase: Buy for required capacity if economics work at the conservative115/hour case. Do not justify the purchase solely by superlinear cost savings. At8x whole-system hourly cost, central accepted-video cost is approximately unchanged versus today’s cold run and about8% higher than the estimated same-SKU warm baseline, assuming equal use and acceptance.

measured_baseline.workload: 49.408-second podcast;1186 deliveredframes;20 independent anchoredchunks;twoPika steps;fastSA2/SA3 plusNVFP4VAE;fullvalidation andextraQA
measured_baseline.baseline_limit: Fresh model/process lifecycle per video;resident loaders across chunks. Historical cross-video two-job test exists for older chained10 configuration, not fast20.

service_assumptions.P: Central15s preserves the measured approximately13.2–13.7s conditioning-node work, including first-prompt encoding, and allows wrappers. It removes process/bootstrap costs from22.8s cold preparation; it does not assume cache hits across distinct customer prompts. Conservative20s,optimistic14s.
service_assumptions.T: Central106s rounds103.9665s extrapolated fast isolated GPU-call work plus1.9702s observed per-chunk wrapper cost. Conservative114s allows length-ratio mismatch and staging variation;optimistic100s assumes a further~6% improvement versus the central service demand from scheduling/residency/batching.
service_assumptions.V: Central45s rounds44.6885s extrapolated fast isolated call work. Approximately21s of historical per-video chunk save/probe/validation wall time is placed in the CPU/output pipeline, not erased. Conservative52s allows~16% extra decode demand;optimistic40s assumes~11% reduction, e.g. avoiding recurring projection-copy/setup work or batching. Those extra gains are hypotheses.
service_assumptions.CPU: Sufficient independent host encoding/validation workers must sustain at least175 completedvideos/hour, with bounded queues. Current background-encoding mechanism is a precedent, but this aggregate rate is assumed, not measured. Same frame/audio/quality acceptance criteria apply.
service_assumptions.efficiency: 85/90/97% are explicit engineering allowances for load imbalance, role transitions, launch gaps and scheduling; they are not experimentally fitted scaling efficiencies.
service_assumptions.SKU: 90/95/100% are target-SKU sensitivities relative to the measured600W workstation. Published server bandwidth1597GB/s versus workstation1792GB/s motivates checking a penalty but does not measure H3 speed. No additional penalty is charged elsewhere.
service_assumptions.single_warm: Estimated single-GPU warm interval D/0.95; targetSKU additionally divides by g. Five percent allows schedule/transition gaps with CPU tails overlapped. These are constructed comparable warm service estimates, not measured sustainable throughput.

capacity_model.formula: I = max(P/(eta*g), T/(5*eta*g), (P+V)/(3*eta*g), C_CPU, C_storage, C_link, C_scheduler). One preparation-capable GPU shares its spare time with VAE tasks; two further GPUs run VAE tasks. CPU and link capacities are not GPU-scaled.
capacity_model.precise_formula: I = max(P/(eta*g), T/(5*eta*g), (P+V)/(3*eta*g), C_CPU, C_storage, C_link, C_scheduler). One preparation-capable GPU shares its spare time with VAE tasks; two further GPUs run VAE tasks. CPU and link capacities are not GPU-scaled.
capacity_model.physical_mapping: Central ideal interval21.2s:GPU0 performs15s preparation plus6.2s VAE work;GPU1/2 each perform19.4s VAE work;GPU3–7 each perform21.2s transformer work. These are average service budgets over several videos. Whole chunks and whole preparation jobs are scheduled discretely;the10%efficiency allowance covers imperfect packing. No arbitrary fractionalGPU splitting is required.
capacity_model.queue_requirement: Keep several videos in flight so the mixedGPU can decode prior-video chunks while preparation for later videos is scheduled. Bounded queues and backpressure protect latency and memory. One isolated video will not fill the steady pipeline.

fixed_role_fallback.meaning: About137/hour,7.6x currentcold if preparationGPU cannotlend sparetime to decoding. This is the simpler initialimplementation.

fluid_pool_reference.note: 148.3/hour requires moreflexible three-role assignment;not used as centralrecommendation.

capacity_model.upper_sensitivity: With optimisticP14,T100,V40,97%pool efficiency and noSKUpenalty, the recommended layout reaches174.6/hour,9.72xcold. Removing all those residual overheads gives180/hour,10.02xcold for thisT100/5 layout. This is a conditional model limit, not an absolute hardwarebound;morekernel optimization or changing roles can change it. Do not budget16x or20x from these timings.

latency.method: OfflineLPT schedule of20 calibrated-shape transformer tasks on5GPUs after15s prep;VAE on3GPUs;GPUservice scaled by0.9*0.95;add1.3s finalchunkencode plus measured6.40s assembly/fullvalidation and4.22s extraQA. No admissionqueue, no freshmodelstartup.
latency.user_interpretation: Approximately55–65s for an individual warm video in this illustration, versus one completion every24.8s under steady load. Throughput8.1x does not mean8.1x per-video latency.

transfer_and_memory.payload_provenance: Old DEFAULT serializedprepared+latent files;proxy only,excludes models/decodedframes andadditional copies.
transfer_and_memory.method: Model transport as a link/serializer capacity and overlap it across chunks/jobs. Do not add the whole per-video transfer time to every pipeline cycle unless synchronization actually forces it. Coarse transfers are small at these rates;host-staging bursts,NUMA,storage and CPU serialization need allowance.
transfer_and_memory.memory: Central mixedGPU needs preparation andVAE models concurrently resident. Existing measured fullfast1T+2V peak43.904GiB and isolated T28.757GiB/V9.061GiB suggest ample96GB capacity for simplerP/V colocation, but this is not a measured combined residency envelope. The implementation must keep preparation alive instead of its currentexit and avoid waitingforanemptyGPU between stages.
transfer_and_memory.interconnect: ServerGPU isPCIe5x16 with noNVLink. CUDA P2P must be verified for actualGPU pairs;host-staged asynchronous copies remain anoption. No per-layer tensorcollectives are assumed.
transfer_and_memory.power: Assumes rated600W cards with sustained cooling and adequateCPU/RAM/NVMe. Eightboards have4.8kW aggregatepower ceilings beforehost/fans;450W orMaxQ configurations need newtiming factors.

economic_formula: cost_per_accepted_video=H/(q*u*y). Requiredthroughputmultiplier forlowercost is(H8/H1)*(u1*y1)/(u8*y8). H iswhole-system amortizedhourlycost;u productiveuse;y acceptanceyield. Noactualquote supplied.
validation: No newGPU runs. Numericalderivation usesrawisolated20 children andpaired73framecalibration;scenarios areinternallycalculated. Largestuncertainties arecross-lengthfastVAE ratio,targetSKU throughput,mixedP/V transitions and aggregateCPUtailcapacity.
